currentContext.business: Fredun Pharmaceuticals is a Palghar (Maharashtra)-based pharmaceutical manufacturer and exporter with deep distributor relationships across 52 countries, supplying branded and OEM generics to semi-regulated and emerging export markets as well as India. Beyond its core Fredun Gx branded-generics business, the Company has diversified into pet healthcare (Freossi, One Pet Stop, Wagr Retail), nutraceuticals (Fredun Nutrition: Mamalait, Fredmax), cosmeceuticals (BeautyFred), mobility & rehabilitation devices (Chuu Balm, BraceOn, NebOn, DigiOn) and premium wellness/specialty therapeutics (DAULCÉL, Hormone Health Products).

currentContext.strengths: Nearly four decades of pharmaceutical operating heritage with deep distributor relationships across 52 countries|Strategy of owning or co-owning product registrations (over 813 held, 1,426 more under development), creating long-term IP value and stronger customer retention/market access|Integrated pet-care ecosystem combining therapeutics, diagnostics, functional foods, retail and services (Freossi + One Pet Stop + Wagr Retail) described by management as a platform few competitors currently offer in India|Pharmaceutical heritage and formulation expertise leveraged to differentiate nutraceutical (Fredun Nutrition) and cosmeceutical (BeautyFred) brands from commodity supplement/beauty players|Approximately 65% of export revenue generated through the Company's own Fredun Gx branded portfolio rather than pure OEM, supporting margin resilience and earnings visibility
currentContext.strategies: Transforming from a traditional pharmaceutical manufacturer into a diversified healthcare platform with growth engines across Pharmaceuticals, Pet Healthcare, Nutraceuticals, Cosmeceuticals, Mobility & Rehabilitation, Healthcare Retail, Premium Wellness and Specialty Therapeutics.|Strategy anchored on leveraging nearly four decades of pharmaceutical expertise while expanding into high-growth healthcare, wellness and consumer-health categories.|Export strategy built on owning or co-owning product registrations across 52 countries to create long-term IP value and strengthen customer retention/market access, alongside strategic OEM partnerships.|Building an integrated pet-care ecosystem (Freossi, One Pet Stop, Wagr Retail) spanning veterinary therapeutics, diagnostics, functional foods, ambulance services, grooming, retail and wellness.|Entering longevity/wellness and specialty therapeutics through the launch of DAULCEL (premium longevity and wellness platform) and Hormone Range Products (advanced performance, preventive health and specialised therapeutics).|Executing a capacity-expansion strategy (new industrial plot, fifth manufacturing facility, additional facility expansion) to build a scalable, future-ready manufacturing infrastructure at Palghar.|Next phase of growth focused on scaling high-potential businesses, strengthening brand equity, expanding global reach, and improving working-capital management and balance-sheet strength.|For FY26 the Board recommended a dividend of 7% on equity shares. At the 39th AGM the Company also proposed to increase Authorised Share Capital from Rs 10 crore to Rs 50 crore and to issue Bonus Equity Shares, alongside a stated management focus on improving working-capital management and strengthening the balance sheet; Infomerics upgraded the Company's credit rating to IVR BBB+ (Stable Outlook) during the year, which management cites as evidence of its capital discipline.
currentContext.expansion: During FY26, Fredun continued strategic investments in manufacturing infrastructure to support growing domestic and international demand. As part of its long-term capacity-expansion strategy, the Company acquired an approximately 76,000 sq. ft. industrial plot in Palghar, Maharashtra; announced its fifth manufacturing facility (initial 40,000 sq. ft. built-up area) designed to support veterinary healthcare products, nutraceuticals, specialty pharmaceutical formulations, wellness products and export-oriented manufacturing, expected to become operational in October 2026; and undertook an additional 12,000 sq. ft. facility expansion to enhance production flexibility and support future capacity requirements. At present the Company operates a single integrated manufacturing facility serving diverse product segments with shared production infrastructure; with successful execution of the planned expansion it expects to emerge as one of India's largest single-location healthcare manufacturing facilities by FY28. Separately, within Pet Healthcare (Freossi) the Company commissioned a specialised functional-foods manufacturing facility and launched India's first 24x7 pet diagnostic centre during the year, while the BeautyFred cosmeceutical business scaled its dedicated manufacturing facility to produce over one million bottles.
currentContext.mdna: India's position as the 'Pharmacy of the World', supplying over 20% of global generic medicines by volume, supports Fredun's established export presence and international reach.|Demand for affordable, quality generic medicines continues to expand across Africa, the Middle East, CIS countries, Southeast Asia and Latin America.|Indian pet-care market projected to grow at approximately 17.1% CAGR, significantly outpacing broader consumer healthcare categories, underpinning the Freossi/pet-healthcare growth thesis.|Indian nutraceutical market expected to grow at approximately 13.5% CAGR through 2030, supporting Fredun Nutrition's expansion.|India's beauty and personal-care e-commerce market projected to grow at approximately 25% CAGR, supporting BeautyFred's cosmeceutical positioning.|Mobility/home-healthcare demand driven by demographic changes, rising incidence of orthopaedic conditions and growing preference for home-based healthcare solutions.|Export revenue growth led by strong demand across semi-regulated and emerging markets, with approximately 65% of export revenue generated through Fredun's own branded (Fredun Gx) portfolio versus OEM partnerships.|Government programmes such as Ayushman Bharat, the PLI Scheme and PMBJP continue to enhance healthcare accessibility and strengthen domestic manufacturing capabilities, benefiting the pharmaceutical sector.|Management believes the diversified, multi-segment approach across pharmaceuticals, pet healthcare, nutraceuticals, consumer wellness, specialty retail and home healthcare enhances resilience and broadens addressable markets.|Registration pipeline: over 813 product registrations currently held globally, with more than 1,426 additional registrations under development.|Successful execution of the TNMSC institutional tender programme during FY26, reflecting institutional-supply traction for the Generics business.

risks.note: Fredun operates in a highly regulated and dynamic healthcare environment; management names regulatory compliance as one of its primary risk areas, relevant given the Company's reliance on maintaining and expanding hundreds of product registrations across export markets.

Named as a primary risk area; quality-system lapses could jeopardize both the regulated/semi-regulated export generics business and the newer consumer-facing brands (pet healthcare, nutraceuticals, cosmeceuticals) that depend on quality-led positioning.
Named as a primary risk area; the Company states it manages this through diversified sourcing, implying meaningful dependence on external supply inputs across its manufacturing operations.
Named as a primary risk area and reiterated in the cautionary/forward-looking statement; material given the Company's export-led Generics business serving international markets.

risks.risk: Execution risk in emerging growth businesses
risks.note: Management explicitly flags 'execution of emerging growth businesses' as a primary risk area — the newer Pet Healthcare, Nutraceuticals, Cosmeceuticals, Mobility & Rehabilitation, Premium Wellness and Specialty Therapeutics verticals are less proven than the legacy Generics franchise and carry scale-up/ramp risk.
